myth: Blocking GPTBot keeps your site out of ChatGPT
fact: GPTBot only collects training data. ChatGPT search uses OAI-SearchBot and live answers use ChatGPT-User, each with its own robots.txt token. A GPTBot rule touches neither.

myth: robots.txt stops ChatGPT-User from opening your pages
fact: OpenAI says robots.txt rules may not apply to ChatGPT-User, because a person asked for the page. Perplexity-User and Meta-ExternalFetcher work the same way.

myth: Blocking Google-Extended hurts you in Google Search
fact: Google says Google-Extended doesn't affect inclusion or ranking in Search. It controls Gemini training and Gemini grounding, not AI Overviews or AI Mode.

myth: No Google-Extended hits in your logs means the block failed
fact: Google-Extended sends no requests of its own. Google crawls with Googlebot and reads the token from robots.txt, so a server or CDN rule on that user agent blocks nothing.

myth: anthropic-ai and Claude-Web are Anthropic's crawlers
fact: Anthropic's docs list only ClaudeBot, Claude-SearchBot and Claude-User. Rules for the old names don't reach any current Claude crawler.

myth: Anthropic doesn't publish IP addresses for its bots
fact: It does, at claude.com/crawling/bots.json. A request from an address on that list is from Anthropic.

myth: Google-NotebookLM is the token for NotebookLM
fact: It's now Google-GeminiNotebook. Rules for the old name stop working once Google drops it.
